hook.title: SSG, SSR, ISR or SPA. Per route, in one line.
hook.lede: `@pyreon/zero` lets every route pick how it renders, prints what it chose at build time, and hydrates by adopting the server's DOM, so what your users typed before the JavaScript landed is still there. Compiled server rendering runs 6.5× faster than React 19 at 1,000 rows (one run).

sections.title: One export per route.
sections.text: The app mode is only the default. A page, or a `_layout` that cascades to everything below it, declares its own mode. Prefer policy in one place? `routeRules` maps path globs to modes.

blocks.label: npm run build
blocks.code:
[zero] Route modes (app: ssr) — 5 ssr λ · 1 ssg ○
  λ ssr  /
  ○ ssg  /about  (declared)
  λ ssr  /counter
  λ ssr  /dashboard
  λ ssr  /posts
  λ ssr  /posts/:id

sections.caption: Precedence is always the same: the page's own `renderMode`, the nearest `_layout`, `routeRules`, `mode: 'auto'` inference, then the app mode. Impossible combinations fail the build and name the route.

sections.title: Or let Zero decide.
sections.text: `mode: 'auto'` is experimental. It infers a mode per route on a "static unless the code says otherwise" rule, and the build prints the table so you can see every choice.

items.title: `getStaticPaths` export
items.text: SSG, even next to a loader.

items.title: Inferred-SSG routes prerender in mixed apps
items.text: In a build that also has SSR routes, pages inferred as SSG are now prerendered, and one resolver answers "what mode does this page get" everywhere. New on main, shipping in the next release.

sections.title: Hydration that keeps what you typed.
text: A slow train, a server-rendered page, three letters typed into the search box. Then the JavaScript lands and a hydrating framework that rebuilds the DOM throws the letters away, along with the cursor.

Pyreon adopts the server's nodes instead of replacing them. Text typed into an uncontrolled input, focus, scroll position inside adopted regions and listeners other scripts attached early all survive the boot. Zero resolves the current route's code before hydrating, so the first client render is the real page, not a loading fallback.

sections.title: Deploy where you already deploy.
sections.text: `--adapter` on `npm create @pyreon/zero@latest` writes the platform files and wires the adapter into `vite.config.ts`.

items.title: `node` and `bun`
items.text: A production server plus a Dockerfile.

items.title: `static`
items.text: Just `dist/`. The scaffolder refuses it with SSR or ISR, because there is no server to run them.

sections.title: Content and a blog, built in.
sections.text: `@pyreon/zero-content` turns `.md` and `.mdx` into real Pyreon JSX at build time, with typed collections, Shiki highlighting, callouts, search and inline live examples. It powers the Pyreon docs and blog.

items.title: Typed collections
items.text: `getCollection`, `getEntry` and `getEntries` query your content with types.

items.title: Scheduled publishing
items.text: Declare `publishDate: 'date'` on a collection and a future-dated entry stays out of listings, search, the sitemap and the feed of a production build until its date; `unpublished: 'omit'` keeps it out of the bundle too. `PYREON_CONTENT_NOW=<date>` builds the site as it will look that day. New on main, shipping in the next release.

items.title: Feeds
items.text: Full-content RSS with `content: 'full'`, the shape dev.to's "Publishing from RSS" imports. New on main, shipping in the next release.

sections.title: From scaffold to a running server.

items.title: Scaffold
items.text: Pick a mode and an adapter, or take the defaults.

items.title: Build
items.text: Every SSG, SSR, ISR or auto build prints its per-route mode table.

items.title: Run
items.text: The Node adapter writes a `node:http` server.

items.a: Yes: `ssr: { mode: 'stream' }`. The default is buffered string rendering.

items.q: What if a prerendered file goes missing?
items.a: The Node and Bun servers serve SSG pages from disk first and fall back to rendering the page, never to a 404.

items.q: Will a typo in my config fail quietly?
items.a: No. Config typos fail with a did-you-mean.
It is labelled experimental. The build table shows exactly what it chose, and an explicit `renderMode` export always wins, so you can pin any route.
